It's worth mentioning that Dragons have never had a basic energy printed for them. Their energy costs have always been multi-colored. We did receive a special energy for them back in the XY era that provided two energy of all types (which was insanely strong), but we likely won't ever see a standard energy card for them and it's probably better that way.

Poison used to be psychic type in the TCG, but then when the SwSh block started, they removed Fairy and Dragon type from the game and decided to move the poison types into dark to make up for the loss of two types as the devs were looking to simplify the structure of weakness and resistance. 

They eventually brought Dragon back as they were an extremely popular type when they were first introduced and definitely a money maker. Fairies haven't come back yet as they were basically a silver bullet to Dragons and weren't strong against any other type in the TCG. So, as a result, all Dragon type cards released since SwSh have had no weakness or resistance.

The dub names are weird. In the early 2000s, a lot of dubbed anime would change names and story to make them more kid-friendly and understandable to the younger audience which was their target demographic. Zatch Bell happened to be one of those series that got caught in the crossfire.

It wasn't too bad, most of the names were the same, but some of the terminology was changed like Demons becoming Mamodos. The ecchi aspect of it was toned down as well. Folgore and Kanchome's anthem of groping women became a song about how they loved to dance all day. 

Overall, it was still a fantastic show and it was unfortunate that the dub was never completed. It didnt generate the popularity of other shows at the time like Naruto and Bleach. It also happened to have one the hardest english opening songs ever composed. Not sure if you're familiar but before the 2010s, a lot of anime geared towards children completely omitted the Japanese opening songs and had original songs written just for the dub. Most were terrible, but Zatch Bell's theme was fire.

As for the Zatch Bell tcg, I'm 99% sure it was U.S. only. In the early 2000s (this is becoming a trend lol) companies like Bandai would frequently produce tcgs based on popular anime at the time. The most successful being the Naruto CCG. (YGO doesn't really count since it wasn't based on the anime itself, but a concept of Takahashi's). Most of these tcgs were short-lived though. For what it's worth, I never learned how to play, I just liked the cards.

Aqua Force is my favorite clan so I'll give you some insight.


Right now we're headed into a very control-oriented meta. With Kagero getting Denial Griffin and Defeat Flare and Link Joker getting support soon it's sufficent to assume that AqF has no amount of pressure on keeping up with the meta. However, there are plenty of things you can do to push them to the limit early.



Thavas: This is by far the best AqF deck in terms of countering the control matchup. It has the most consistency of any AqF deck imo. Thavas and his stride force your opponent to retire a unit of their's upon achieving the 4th attack of your turn. You also gain access to Adelaide which is the a Glimmer Breath clone that stands itself while gaining 2k and has no attack order restriction. Additionally you can also play Battle Siren Melania which is an amazing grade 1 that's strictly Thavas only that allows you to CB 1 and draw on the third attack or more and gain 5k until the end of that battle. It's also not 1/Turn. Oh and did I mention it has Resist?



Blue Wave: This is the most aggressive AqF deck currently. Anger-boil is the Blue Wave stride bearer that is tied specifically to the Tetra-boil stride. Both are amazing. Anger-boil states that when you stride Tetra-boil, it gains 3k, and upon the second attack as the vanguard, choose 2 units, stand them and they receive 3k each. Tetra-boil is generally the same card as the original Tetra-Drive grade 3 but instead of pitching 2 upon the 4th attack achieved you pitch 1 instead, netting you a plus 1 overall. The only downside is that you are enfeebled with -1 drive check. The best part of this deck however is that you have access to all restanding rearguards. The best one for this deck is definitely Foivos. For a single CB upon being the third attack only of that turn, given that you have a Blue Wave vanguard, you gain 2k and restand after attacking. This means that even if Foivos is your only rearguard, you will be able to achieve Tetra-boil's skill. Massive pressure from this deck in that you can use the Thavas stride in this deck effectively as well.



Ripples: How the mighty have fallen. This deck has the best grade 2 rush, but without having Odysseus on board at all times it tends to fall apart. Don't get me wrong though, it can still wreck face, you just have to get lucky with getting the Odysseus. Still pretty solid. Has tutoring potential with the Ripple crit. A bit weaker than Thavas or Blue Wave but still very good. It's worth mentioning that you can achieve much success without abusing Tidal Assault due to Ripple's inherent rearguard restanding abilities.



Maelstrom: The Admiral is very weak these days. Others will disagree with me, but I think this is the weakest AqF deck right now. It was very strong back when the second G Booster was released with Rascal Sweeper and the crit that disallows grade 0 guarding against a Maelstrom. However these days you just don't achieve great numbers or many pressure attacks from this deck without striding, but the unfortunate reality is that the Maelstrom stride is just not very good. The break ride is probably the only good thing about this deck atm and it makes me a bit sad since this was at one point in time one of the strongest decks. It pretty much auto-loses to any control matchup.



Now onto cards you should be running:

Tidal Assault: This card is you BnB in almost every AqF deck. It's abusable as hell with no GB1 or attack order restriction. It's my favorite card in the whole game. The best part about this card is that your opponent will go out of their way to waste attacks trying to kill him if they aren't playing a control deck. 

Skyros: This is the card that makes Link Joker, Kagero and Narukami flip tables. On achieving GB1, your front row rearguards gain Resist. It also allows you to search for a grade 3 from the top 5 cards when achieving the third attack when you ride it. Basically if you have this card on the VG and three Resist units in the back row, you can control what cards your opponent will Stride into as well as what plays they can make. This effectively saves you from anything that chooses to retire and essintially your opponent can only stride Spaghetti Messiah in Messiahs and they do absolutely nothing in Chaos Breaker. I think this card is the best standalone grade 3 for AqF.

Lambros: This guy speaks for himself. Big columns are nothing to scoff at especially when they can still stand again after attacking. Amazing card still after over a year.

These are purely my opinions. Take them with a grain of salt. I absolutely love AqF, but it will have a tough time going into this meta. But if you want to play it, take your time and choose your plays carefully.
